answer: Because the timing is recorded against the crystal challenge, the wharf audit can replay the tide history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 39 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A scripted farm thus has to pad 188 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
